title: quartodown
text:
quartodown is an R package that turns your package’s README, help pages and vignettes into a website, rendered entirely by Quarto.


pkgdown can render Quarto vignettes, but it replaces Quarto’s styling with its own (theme: "none", minimal: TRUE). As a result, Quarto features such as callout blocks, code annotations and tabsets don’t render correctly; callouts, for instance, become plain blockquotes.
quartodown renders the whole site with Quarto itself, so you get:

full Quarto support, on every page;
a package website layout: a home page sidebar, a grouped function reference, articles and a changelog;
function links with hover tooltips.




Install from GitHub:
pak::pak("https://github.com/BjarkeHautop/quartodown")



Browse around to see how it looks! Quarto features shows callouts, tabsets, footnotes and more on a quartodown site. If you like what you see, and want to use it for your own package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown.yml, with a reference: field that lists your package’s current functions in one section; edit it to group them however you’d like. It also gitignores the files the build generates.
Then build the site:
quartodown::build_site()
A preview can then be viewed using quartodown::preview_site().
The navbar is built from your vignettes: the one named after the package (or the only top-level one) becomes “Get started”, and the rest, including those in vignettes/articles/, go under “Articles”. See ?quartodown::build_site for everything quartodown.yml can configure.




jlbind

Using quartodown for your package? Feel free to open a pull request adding it to this list.

build_site(

title: Build the package website
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the package root.




tooltips


Logical. Link references to the package’s own functions (in code blocks and inline code) to their reference page, with a hover tooltip showing the function’s usage and the first sentence of its description?




freeze


Logical. Reuse the results of code that ran in an earlier build, for pages whose source hasn’t changed since? Uses Quarto’s freeze, which keeps them in _quarto/_freeze/.




quiet


Logical. Hide Quarto’s rendering output?




devel


Logical. By default, the examples and vignettes run against the package installed from path into a temporary library. With devel = TRUE, they run against it loaded with pkgload::load_all() instead, which is faster, but code that starts other R processes (e.g. with callr or parallel workers) won’t find the package there.

title: Build the package website
Build the package website
text:
Value

title: Build the package website
text:
Configuration
_quartodown.yml, at the package root, is optional; use_quartodown() creates one. It can contain:


reference: groups the function reference index into sections. It is a list of sections, each with any of:


title: the section heading;


subtitle: a heading one level below it;


desc: Markdown text shown under the heading(s);


contents: the topics listed, in order.


For example:
reference:
  - title: Read and write
    desc: Functions for getting data in and out.
    contents:
      - read_data
      - starts_with("write_")
  - title: Helpers
    contents:
      - has_concept("helpers")
      - -internal_helper
Each contents entry is a topic (an \alias or Rd file name) or a selector: starts_with(), ends_with(), contains() and matches() (a regular expression) match aliases, and has_concept() and has_keyword() match \concepts and \keywords. c() combines selectors, and a leading - removes topics from those selected by the entries above it (or, as the first entry, from all topics). Topics not listed in any section get a warning and are left off the index.
Without reference, every topic is listed in one section. Internal topics (\keyword{internal}) are left out unless named or selected with internal = TRUE, e.g. starts_with("dev_", internal = TRUE); then they get a page too. The format is the same as pkgdown’s reference: field, so an existing one can be copied over.


articles: the order of the "Articles" navbar menu, as vignette paths relative to vignettes/ without extension (e.g. articles/details). Without it, every vignette other than the "Get started" one is listed, top-level vignettes first, then those in vignettes/articles/.


quarto: settings merged over the generated Quarto configuration. Settings are merged key by key: a list of entries (e.g. the navbar’s left: or right: items) is added to, any other value is replaced, and ~ removes a setting. For example, to add a navbar link:
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com


The "Get started" link points to the vignette named after the package, or to the only top-level vignette if there is just one.

title: Technical details
text: quartodown generates a Quarto website project from the package sources, so the man pages, vignettes and generated pages are all Quarto pages, and every Quarto feature works.

title: Technical details
text:
How a build works
quartodown::build_site() runs in three stages:

Before rendering, it installs the package into a temporary library and writes a Quarto project into _quarto/. With build_site(devel = TRUE), each page’s R process loads it from source with pkgload::load_all() instead.1
During rendering, Quarto renders _quarto/ into docs/, running the examples and vignette code against that package.
After rendering, it links code to its documentation and adds hover tooltips.

The only file you edit is _quartodown.yml. _quarto/ is rewritten on every build, and gitignored by quartodown::use_quartodown():
_quarto/
├── _quarto.yml                   # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                      # home page
├── reference/
│   ├── index.qmd                 # function reference index
│   └── <topic>.qmd               # a page per man/*.Rd
├── authors.qmd                   # authors and citation page
├── vignettes/                    # the vignettes, as they are
├── man/figures/                  # images for the README and man pages
├── NEWS.md                       # changelog, with issues and users linked
├── quartodown.scss               # theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── quartodown-header.html        # dark-mode default
├── quartodown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment
└── orcid.svg, ror.svg            # icons for authors' ORCID/ROR ids
Reference pages are served at reference/<topic>.html, and docs/pkgdown.yml lets downlit on other sites link to them.

title: Technical details
text:
Before rendering

The home page
index.md holds the README next to a sidebar with links, the license, the citation, the developers and the README’s badges.
A README <picture> with light and dark versions shows the one matching the site’s theme.


The reference index
To group and order the function index, use the reference: field in _quartodown.yml:
reference:
1  - title: Building the site
2    desc: >
      Set up a package, then build its site.
    contents:
3      - use_quartodown
4      - starts_with("build_")

1

Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.

2

An optional description, shown under the heading.

3

A topic, by any of its \alias{} names.

4

A selector: starts_with(), ends_with(), contains(), matches(), has_concept(), has_keyword(), - to exclude and c() to combine.


build_site() warns about any topic the index leaves out, except \keyword{internal} ones. An internal topic is listed, and gets a page, only when named, as with roxygen’s reexports, or selected with internal = TRUE, as in starts_with("dev_", internal = TRUE).


The navbar and footer
The navbar links the “Get started” vignette, the reference index, the other vignettes under “Articles” and the changelog. The footer has a “Developed by …” line, built from Authors@R.


Code output
R output is shown in the same block as the code, prefixed with #>. To show a chunk’s output in a block of its own, set #| collapse: false on it.






TipChanging the Quarto configuration



A quarto: field in _quartodown.yml is merged over the generated configuration. Lists, like the navbar’s items, are appended to; any other setting is replaced, and ~ removes it. For example, to add a navbar link and fold code blocks:
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true

title: Technical details
text:
The man pages
Each man/*.Rd file, except \keyword{internal} ones the reference index doesn’t list, becomes a reference page, rendered with the package’s Rd macros (such as Rdpack’s \insertRef{}). Build-stage \Sexpr{} macros run with the package installed, as in R CMD build, though not with devel = TRUE.

Usage, the usage of R6 methods, and code blocks with a language, such as roxygen’s ```yaml, are syntax-highlighted with a copy button.
Links go to the topic’s reference page, or, for another package’s topic, to its documentation as downlit finds it.
Math in \eqn{} and \deqn{} is rendered.
Examples run, with their output in the same block. \dontrun{} code is shown but not run, \dontshow{} code is run but not shown, and @examplesIf examples run only if their condition holds.

title: Technical details
text:
After rendering
downlit links function calls in R code blocks, and inline code like mean(), to their documentation. In blocks with code annotations, only function calls and %op% operators such as %in% are linked.
References to the package’s own functions also get a hover tooltip with their usage and the first sentence of their description. Try it: hover over build_site() or use_quartodown(). build_site() warns when a first sentence is longer than 200 characters, since the tooltip cuts it off. To build without tooltips, use build_site(tooltips = FALSE).

title: Technical details
text:
The theme
The site uses Quarto’s default theme in light mode and darkly in dark mode, with quartodown.scss on top of each:
theme:
  light: [default, quartodown.scss]
  dark: [darkly, quartodown.scss]
quartodown.scss gives both modes the same font and heading sizes, so switching modes doesn’t shift the text. quartodown-header.html and quartodown-after-body.html also:

show the dark theme to new visitors whose system is set to dark mode,
line up the navbar title with the page text,
show the version number smaller next to the package name,
leave #> output lines out when copying code.

title: Technical details
text:
Footnotes


devel = TRUE may not work if your examples or vignettes start other R processes, for example with callr or parallel.↩︎

title: Quarto features
text: quartodown renders every page with Quarto itself, so all of Quarto’s authoring features work in your vignettes and articles. This page shows some of them as they look on a quartodown site. View the source of this page to see how each one is written.

title: Quarto features
text:
Callouts






Note



Callouts draw attention to a piece of text. There are five types: note, tip, important, warning and caution.








TipTip with a title



Give a callout a title with a heading as its first line.








WarningClick to expand





Callouts can be collapsible, which is handy for details most readers can skip.

title: Quarto features
text:
Tabsets
Tabsets show alternative views of the same thing, one at a time:

SummaryPlotBy cylinders



summary(mtcars$mpg)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   10.40   15.43   19.20   20.09   22.80   33.90




hist(mtcars$mpg, main = NULL, xlab = "Miles per gallon", col = "steelblue")











aggregate(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars, FUN = mean)
#>   cyl      mpg
#> 1   4 26.66364
#> 2   6 19.74286
#> 3   8 15.10000

title: Quarto features
text:
Function links
Functions from this package are linked to their reference page, with a tooltip on hover, both inline, like build_site(), and in code:

build_site(devel = TRUE)
preview_site()

In code, functions from other packages are linked to their own documentation by downlit, like summary() in the tabset above.

Footnotes and margin content
Footnotes are written with [^name].1 Quarto shows them at the end of the page, and as a popup when you hover over the reference.
Content can also be placed in the margin.


This note sits in the margin, next to the paragraph it belongs to.

title: Get started with quartodown
text: quartodown builds a website for an R package with Quarto. This guide sets up a package, builds its site, and publishes it on GitHub Pages.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Set up
From the root of your package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown.yml at the package root, the configuration file you can edit, and adds the files the build generates to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Build the site
quartodown::build_site()
quartodown::preview_site()
build_site() builds the site into docs/, and preview_site() opens it in your browser. Examples and vignettes run against your package’s current source. While iterating, build_site(devel = TRUE) is faster because it loads the package with pkgload::load_all() instead of installing it.
The following is added to your site:

Home page: your README.md. Next to it, a sidebar links to the source code, the bug tracker and CRAN (if the package is there), and shows the license, citation and authors from DESCRIPTION. Any badges in your README (between <!-- badges: start --> and <!-- badges: end -->) are moved into the sidebar.
Reference: a page for each help topic in man/, plus an index page listing them all.
Get started: the vignette with the same name as your package, like this one.
Articles: all your other vignettes, including any in vignettes/articles/.
Changelog: your NEWS.md. Issue numbers like #123 and GitHub usernames like @user become links.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Organize the reference index
By default the reference index lists every function in one section. To group them, edit the reference: field in _quartodown.yml:
reference:
  - title: Setting up
    contents:
      - use_quartodown
  - title: Building
    contents:
      - starts_with("build_")
See ?build_site for the other fields.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Publish on GitHub Pages
To build the site and deploy it to the gh-pages branch on every push, add a GitHub Actions workflow:
quartodown::use_quartodown_action()
This writes .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml. Commit and push it. Once its first run has created the gh-pages branch, go to the Pages section of your repository’s settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that branch.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Learn more
Quarto features shows Quarto’s authoring features, such as callouts, tabsets and footnotes, on a quartodown site.
Technical details explains how a build works and how quartodown’s theme is put together.

Usage

title: Set up a package to use quartodown

Arguments



path


Path to the target package root. Defaults to the current directory.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Details
An existing _quartodown.yml is never overwritten.
use_quartodown() adds the following lines to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore (only the ones not already present in each file):

# .gitignore
_quarto/*
!_quarto/_freeze/

# .Rbuildignore
^docs$
^_quarto$
^_quartodown\.yml$


_quarto/ is the Quarto project build_site() generates and renders into docs/. Its _freeze/ directory holds the results of code run with build_site(freeze = TRUE), which can be committed so later builds, e.g. on CI, reuse them.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to _quartodown.yml.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Examples

pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_quartodown(pkg)
#> ✔ Wrote '/tmp/RtmpdIxL32/examplepkg192a5ecccbaf/_quartodown.yml' (edit this to group your functions).
#> ✔ Added `_quarto/*` and `!_quarto/_freeze/` to '/tmp/RtmpdIxL32/examplepkg192a5ecccbaf/.gitignore'.
#> ✔ Added `^docs$`, `^_quarto$`, and `^_quartodown\.yml$` to '/tmp/RtmpdIxL32/examplepkg192a5ecccbaf/.Rbuildignore'.
#> 
#> Next steps:
#> 1. Edit '_quartodown.yml' to group your functions the way you want.
#> 2. Build the site with `quartodown::build_site()`.
#> 3. Preview it with `quartodown::preview_site()`.
readLines(file.path(pkg, "_quartodown.yml"))
#>  [1] "# Configuration for quartodown::build_site(). See ?quartodown::build_site for"
#>  [2] "# all fields, including `articles:` (navbar order) and `quarto:` (extra"      
#>  [3] "# Quarto settings)."                                                          
#>  [4] ""                                                                             
#>  [5] "# Groups the function reference index into sections, each with a `title:`"    
#>  [6] "# and the `contents:` it lists (topic names or selectors such as"             
#>  [7] "# starts_with(\"read_\")). See ?quartodown::build_site for the details."      
#>  [8] "reference:"                                                                   
#>  [9] "  - title: All functions"                                                     
#> [10] "    contents:"                                                                
#> [11] "      []"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)
